skill.name: aws-cost-optimizer
skill.description: Analyze AWS spending and identify optimization opportunities using AWS CLI, Cost Explorer, and CloudWatch data.
skill.summary: Find AWS cost drivers, idle resources, and practical savings opportunities.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static command and network findings are false positives from Markdown examples, fixed date substitutions, JMESPath syntax, and official AWS links. One medium operational risk remains because the workflow recommends actions that can delete or stop AWS resources.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation, backups, dry-run checks, and production change approval before deleting storage or stopping resources.
Document the skill as safe for read-only analysis and medium risk for cleanup or rightsizing actions.
Tell users to verify regions, accounts, resource IDs, tags, and retention requirements before acting on recommendations.

content.value_statement: AWS spending can grow through idle resources, weak tagging, and missed reservation opportunities. This skill guides structured AWS cost analysis and safer optimization planning.
actual_capabilities: Breaks down AWS costs by service, time period, region, and tags.
Identifies idle EC2 instances, unattached EBS volumes, unused Elastic IPs, and old snapshots.
Uses CloudWatch metrics to support EC2 and RDS rightsizing reviews.
Suggests Reserved Instance, Savings Plan, and S3 lifecycle opportunities.
Helps create cost optimization checklists, reports, and monitoring workflows.
limitations: Requires AWS CLI access, valid credentials, and permissions for Cost Explorer and CloudWatch.
Example commands may need account, region, tag, and resource ID changes.
Cannot prove a resource is unused without workload and business context.
Deletion and rightsizing recommendations need human review before production changes.

use_cases.title: Monthly Cost Review
use_cases.description: Summarize AWS spending trends, top services, anomalies, and savings candidates for a regular review meeting.

use_cases.title: Cloud Waste Cleanup
use_cases.description: Find unattached volumes, unused addresses, idle instances, and old snapshots before a controlled cleanup effort.

use_cases.title: Leadership Savings Plan
use_cases.description: Create an executive summary of savings opportunities, risk levels, and recommended next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review Recent AWS Spend
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my AWS costs for the last 30 days by service. Highlight the largest drivers and explain what changed.

prompt_templates.title: Find Obvious Waste
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me identify unattached EBS volumes, unused Elastic IPs, idle EC2 instances, and old snapshots. Separate safe checks from destructive actions.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Rightsizing Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Review EC2 and RDS utilization data for rightsizing opportunities. Include confidence levels, risks, and validation steps before any change.

prompt_templates.title: Create a FinOps Action Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 90-day AWS cost optimization plan with quick wins, reservation analysis, tagging improvements, budgets, owners, and measurable savings targets.

output_examples.input: Show me the biggest AWS cost drivers for the last month.
output: A ranked service cost summary with month-over-month change.
A short explanation of likely causes for increases.
Recommended follow-up checks for the top spending services.

output_examples.input: Find unused resources that may be safe to clean up.
output: A review list of candidate EBS volumes, Elastic IPs, snapshots, and idle instances.
A risk note for each resource type.
Validation steps to complete before deletion or shutdown.

output_examples.input: Prepare a cost optimization summary for leadership.
output: An executive summary of savings opportunities.
Estimated impact grouped by quick wins and strategic changes.
A clear action plan with owners, risks, and next review dates.

best_practices: Start with read-only analysis before planning any cleanup or rightsizing change.
Validate every resource with owners, tags, backups, and retention rules before deletion.
Track expected savings, actual savings, and operational impact after each change.
anti_patterns: Deleting volumes or snapshots only because they appear unused in one query.
Changing production instance sizes without workload testing and rollback plans.
Ignoring tagging, budgets, and anomaly alerts after a one-time cleanup.

faq.question: Does this skill make changes to my AWS account?
faq.answer: The documented analysis steps are mostly read-only, but the skill also discusses cleanup actions. Review and approve every change yourself.

faq.question: What AWS permissions are needed?
faq.answer: You need permissions for Cost Explorer, EC2 inventory, CloudWatch metrics, and any services included in your review.

faq.question: Can it find exact savings automatically?
faq.answer: It can estimate likely savings from cost and inventory data. Final savings depend on pricing, commitments, usage, and implementation timing.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production accounts?
faq.answer: It is suitable for read-only production analysis. Use change management, backups, and approvals before production cleanup or rightsizing.

faq.question: Does it support multi-account AWS organizations?
faq.answer: It can guide multi-account reviews if your AWS CLI profile and permissions expose the required cost and resource data.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools for this skill.
